title: The Unwritten Lantern
premise: In the river town of Vessengard, 1848, Edmund Oyelaran works the type cases in his father's print shop, convinced that history is something that happens to other people, elsewhere. When the army requisitions the town and seizes the master ledger containing every citizen's name and ration status, Edmund discovers his father has been secretly printing seditious pamphlets — and that the ledger, hidden in the type cases, is now the only proof of who deserves a berth on the last ferry before the river ice breaks. As soldiers close in and the thaw accelerates, Edmund must decide which family member takes the final place: his ailing father, his pregnant sister, or himself, the only one who can carry the ledger to the revolutionary committee across the river. He gives the berth to his sister, stays behind to print one last true account of the requisition, and escapes across the breaking ice with the ledger — at the cost of his father, who is arrested in his place.
about_author: Ulyana Ishikawa is a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century print shops across Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted bindery in Riga, where she still sets type by hand.

chapters.title: The Weight of Letters
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. A quiet portrait of the print shop: Edmund sorting type, his father Augustin cutting a new face, his sister Marta sewing. Edmund dismisses rumors of approaching soldiers as talk for taverns. Emotional beat: comfortable complacency, the warmth of a family that believes itself unremarkable.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Grey-coated soldiers occupy the town square and post an order: all civil registers and ledgers surrendered within three days, on pain of hanging. Augustin goes pale and burns something in the stove that night. Emotional beat: the first crack in Edmund's belief that history happens elsewhere.

chapters.title: What Father Burns
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Marta catches her father feeding pamphlets to the fire and confronts him; he confesses he has been printing for the resistance for two years. She agrees to silence but cannot forgive the lie. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by deception within the family itself.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Type Cases
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Searching for a missing font, Edmund finds the town's master ledger hidden beneath the type cases — names, rations, debts, everything the army wants. He realizes his father is already a dead man if it's found. Emotional beat: dread arriving as a physical weight in the hands.

chapters.title: Captain Voss
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. The requisition officer, Captain Voss, inspects the print shop with unsettling courtesy and orders Edmund to set type for army proclamations. Voss mentions, casually, that the ledger is 'merely administrative.' Emotional beat: the seduction of being seen as useful rather than dangerous.

chapters.title: Names and Rations
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Food grows scarce; the army's ration list omits half the town. Marta, secretly pregnant by a conscripted printer's apprentice, understands her name's absence could mean starvation. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into quiet, practical anger.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Bargain
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. The ferryman Halvard reveals the ice will break within weeks and the army controls all berths — except one private berth he will sell to the highest moral claim. Edmund begins, shamefully, to calculate. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal and arithmetic.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Pressed into printing proclamations by day, Edmund secretly sets a resistance pamphlet by night, learning his father's craft as an act of inheritance and rebellion. Emotional beat: first agency; the thrill and terror of choosing a side.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. A neighbor is arrested after a pamphlet surfaces; Marta suspects someone inside the resistance circle is selling names. She warns her father, who refuses to believe his comrades could betray each other. Emotional beat: truth becoming more dangerous than loyalty.

chapters.title: Voss's Offer
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Voss, having guessed the ledger's hiding place, offers Edmund a deal: the ledger for his family's safe passage on an army barge. Edmund stalls, horrified to find the offer is not obviously wrong. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: Marta's Confession
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Marta tells Edmund about the pregnancy and asks for the ferry berth if it comes to that. Edmund, who had been silently reserving it for himself and the ledger, says nothing. Emotional beat: love against duty, first collision.

chapters.title: Augustin's Argument
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Edmund discovers his father plans to surrender himself and the ledger together, believing a public trial will expose the requisition's cruelty. Edmund argues the trial will simply be a hanging. Emotional beat: a son trying to out-love his father's idealism.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Soldiers raid the shop while Edmund is out; Augustin hides the ledger in the frozen well and is taken for questioning. Marta, alone and pregnant, retrieves it through a hole in the ice. Emotional beat: courage born of having nothing left to protect but truth.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Voss interrogates Edmund with the burned pamphlet fragments on the table, offering again: ledger for family. Edmund, now certain Voss intends to hang them regardless, lies for the first time in his life. Emotional beat: the point of no return, crossed quietly.

chapters.title: Halvard's Price
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Edmund begs Halvard for the last berth; Halvard names his price — not money, but the ledger itself, to buy his own family's passage from the committee across the river. Edmund refuses. Emotional beat: discovering that everything has a price, including the proof of names.

chapters.title: The Night Compositors
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Marta and Edmund set the true account of the requisition — every confiscated name, every withheld ration — planning to scatter copies before the ice breaks. Working side by side, they finally speak of the berth. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Breaking
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. The ice groans and splits at dawn. In the chaos of the army's evacuation, Augustin is paraded for execution as the 'printer of lies.' Edmund must choose in a single breath: save his father or distribute the account. Emotional beat: the choice the whole book has been building, arriving without mercy.

chapters.title: Which Name in the Berth
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Edmund forces Marta onto the ferry with the ledger sewn into her coat, staying behind to run the press one final time. Marta screams his name from the water as the ice carries the boat downstream. Emotional beat: love expressed as an unbearable act of subtraction.

chapters.title: The Last Impression
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Edmund prints the final copies as soldiers breach the shop; Augustin, in chains, sees the pamphlets flying over the square and smiles before the shots. Edmund flees through the print shop's paper cellar toward the river. Emotional beat: climax and sacrifice — the father's idealism vindicated at the highest price.

chapters.title: Across the Water
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Edmund crosses the broken river on drifting ice, half-drowned, clutching a wet copy of the true account. On the far bank, committee men take his deposition and the ledger's testimony begins its work. Emotional beat: hollow survival; the price of survival fully counted.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Weeks later, in the free town, Marta reads the published account with her father's name in it and her brother's deposition beside it. Voss's requisition is exposed; Augustin is posthumously named a printer of record. Emotional beat: truth outlasting loyalty's cost, grief with a floor under it.

chapters.title: Setting the New Face
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. In spring, Edmund cuts a new typeface in his father's style and prints the ledger's names as a book, dedicating the last page to the berth he gave away. Marta's child is born as the edition dries. Emotional beat: resolution — history, Edmund finally understands, is what ordinary people refuse to let be unwritten.
